_note: 2026-07-23 batch (batch 4 of the seminaries/midrashot-only pass). Yield was very low this round: Bnos Binah Seminary (bnosbinahseminary.com) has an expired SSL certificate (effectively a dead site despite domain still resolving); Rav Wolf Seminary (Bnei Brak) and Sha'arei Bina (Tzfat) have no independent official website, only Facebook/directory/aggregator listings (Sha'arei Bina's own-looking domain, shaareibina.org, actually belongs to an unrelated Florida day school of a similar name); HaMidrasha at Oranim's gap-year page returns a genuine 404. Only one new program cleared the bar.

seminaries_midrashot.name: YU Israel Women's Campus
seminaries_midrashot.description: A three-year undergraduate program combining flexible online BBA coursework (Global Business & Innovation) with in-person Torah learning in Jerusalem, for women who have already completed a year of study at a YU-approved seminary or yeshiva.
seminaries_midrashot.durationText: 6 semesters, following 2 semesters at an affiliated Israel seminary/yeshiva
seminaries_midrashot.signupInstructions: Submit transcripts for evaluation via the online form or by emailing yuiprogram@yu.edu.
seminaries_midrashot.adminNote: STRUCTURALLY a post-seminary/continuation program, not a standalone first-year seminary: explicitly requires two semesters already completed at another YU-approved seminary or yeshiva before a student can join. Administrative HQ is YU's New York campus, but the program itself operates in Jerusalem (Nefesh B'Nefesh Residence) with in-person Torah learning there -- included on that basis, same reasoning applied to the already-added 'Midrasha at Bar-Ilan University' and 'Maalot Yerushalayim' (both also require prior/concurrent enrollment elsewhere). Tags mirror that pairing (Academic/Internship + Spiritual growth + Girls only + jerusalem), plus Religious Zionism/Modern Orthodox matching YU's institutional character.
